key_insight: The local tangent residual (LTR) estimates whether turbulent-flow data could benefit from nonlinear compression before training an autoencoder.
engineering_relevance: LTR can help practitioners choose between POD and nonlinear autoencoders, potentially avoiding costly architecture searches and hyperparameter tuning when POD suffices.
method: Compute LTR from local data geometry without model training or a threshold parameter.
Compare LTR trends with autoencoder compression performance.
Quantify trained-decoder nonlinearity using decoder linearisation error (DLE) relative to a linearised surrogate.
evidence_signal: Across two vortex street cases and a turbulent wind-turbine wake, LTR reproduced dominant autoencoder compression trends, while large nonlinear compression potential was corroborated by large DLE.
watch_item: Validation covers three flow datasets; reliability across broader turbulent regimes and data-sampling conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: A Priori Estimation of the Non-Linear Compression Potential and Quantification of Autoencoder Non-Linearity in Turbulent Flows
